series: Climate Fiscal Policy Brief No. 3.2 · October 2026
title: From Projects to Asset Classes

slides.title: From Projects to Asset Classes
slides.subtitle: Two-stage finance and synthetic sovereign bonds for clean power
slides.message: Clean power plants are financed one at a time, on bespoke terms. Split each project at commissioning, pool operating plants under one standard contract and refinance them through first loss, a thin mezzanine and a senior synthetic sovereign bond. The price of solar power falls by about a fifth.
slides.author: Stephen J. Stretton · writing in a personal capacity

slides.text: Payment risk is the first problem (Brief 3.1). Once it is removed, the rest of the premium is packaging: each plant is financed alone, on bespoke documents, by a lender who cannot sell the loan.

slides.title: Real deals carry far thicker cushions, and the saving survives them

points.text: $458m of 37 Asian and Middle Eastern infrastructure loans; 30% of the notes sat below the top class.

points.lead: With a 30% cushion the saving is still 14%;
points.text: 5–8% is where a standard pool with a record ends up, not where it starts. Bayfront's ninth deal (2026) had Aaa/AAA Class A notes.

slides.title: Where there is no contract, guarantee the bond; where savers are local, issue in local currency

points.text: Vietnam curtailed 364 GWh of solar in 2020; South Africa's 2022 auction awarded no wind for lack of grid in the Cape.

conditional on reform: state, then national government, then a donor vehicle. Tiers fail together, so the donor tier is called three times as often at a correlation of 0.5.
gives domestic savers a safe asset, with a thicker cushion or a guarantor such as GuarantCo.
